label: original-phase z after m in 0-initial sequences (sparse conjunction)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.005% of steps). Fires almost only in the original phase (97% of mass), on steps t=4-6, and mostly when the input token is z (76% of mass). It is never active in the copy phase and only weakly at <DEL>. Among z inputs it is highly selective. The strongest activations come when the sequence starts with 0 (first_tok=0 holds 78% of mass) and the previous token is m (prev_tok=m, 67% of mass); the top example is 0 0 m m [z]. The conjunction z & first token 0 & prev m reaches about 0.78 precision at t>=4, but it covers only about 27% of mass. Remaining activations are small, on z (or occasionally other tokens) after m two steps back, or in sequences with many digits. Plain z in the original phase has precision 0.002, so the feature is a conjunction of z, a 0-initial sequence and recent m that no simple predicate captures well (best dev F1 about 0.24).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=0 (+4.50), prev_tok=m (+3.74), prev2_tok=m (+2.30), orig1=0 (+2.24), orig1=1 (+2.02), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=z (+1.76). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-2.75), orig_idx=-1 (-2.17), t=3 (-1.80), in_count=1 (-1.72).
